name: Розрахуй і візьми (1)
description:
Capturing an unprotected piece is usually a good thing. But even if a piece has one or more protectors, it may be a good move to take it.

You have learned before to count attackers and defenders. If there are more attackers than defenders, you can make your capture.
However, good calculation is essential!

Take your time to study the examples.

In a series of captures, it is usually best to capture with the least valuable piece first. The most valuable attacker takes last.

You have practised this before, but now the board is more crowded. This makes is more difficult to find the piece that has more attackers than defenders.
Make sure to scan the whole board, or you might overlook something.

What do you have to do?

Capture a piece that is insufficiently protected and gain material.
Start by finding the piece that is under attack. Then, count the attackers and the protectors.
Are there more attackers than defenders? This generally means that you can win the piece.
Think carefully about which piece to capture with first!

examples.text:
The black bishop protects the knight. But a knight has a higher value than a pawn.
So, White can win points by taking the knight.
It won’t hurt that the bishop will capture White’s pawn.
After trading, White is up in points: 3 (knight) – 1 (pawn) = 2 points.

In this position, White should not capture the knight.
Should his queen take the knight, Black can take the queen with his bishop. White loses points.
Black takes 9 points (queen) and White only 3 (knight): 9-3 = 6 points lost.

Again, the black knight is protected by a bishop.
But now White has two attackers: a knight and the queen.
Black’s knight has only one defender.
As you remember from Pawn Level, you can win a piece if there are more attackers than protectors.

But you must pay close attention to the order in which you move your pieces.
White can take the knight with the bishop or the queen.
Black will recapture with his bishop, but you can take that in return.


Should the queen capture first, your calculation looks like this:
Knight + bishop (3 + 3) = 6 point. But then you lose your queen: minus 9 points. You lose more point than you win. Therefore, this is not a good move.

If the knight takes first, we get this calculation:
Knight + bishop (3 + 3) = 6 point. Then your bishop is taken: minus 3. But you still have 3 points left. This is much better!

texts: Two attackers, one defender? Someone's in trouble!
